lines: A few straps snapped and a few nerves did too, but the village held.
Leather remembers every cut. So do people.
You helped keep more than roofs intact.
The village came through worn, but not torn apart.
I saw courage stretched tight without snapping. Yours included.
Raiders test every weak point. You became a strong one.
I can repair gear. You spared things that cannot be repaired.
The doors and shields held better because you fought.
I have a pile of torn harnesses and every animal that wore one is alive.
Your warning gave us time to bar the tannery windows.
We used spare belts to brace the gate after the hinge broke.
The guards need shield straps fitted to the person carrying them.
I am making simple slings for anyone assigned to move the wounded.
Every shelter should keep blankets and strong cord by the door.
The west fence failed where rain had softened the posts.
We should mark a clear route from the pens to the safest building.
A pack of repair supplies belongs near each gate.
People fought better once they knew their families had reached shelter.
Bring me the damaged gear before small tears become failures.
The next defense begins with the repairs we make today.
